companies.name: Corva AI
companies.description: Corva is a Houston-based AI software company that provides a real-time drilling, completions, geoscience, and sustainability analytics platform for the oil and gas industry. The Corva platform ingests sensor and rig data and exposes it through a RESTful Data API used by E&P operators and service companies. Corva Dev Center is an SDK and app hosting environment that lets customers build frontend, backend, scheduled, and stream applications on top of Corva data assets, with Python and JavaScript SDKs and UI component libraries.

companies.name: Toucan
companies.description: Toucan builds digital infrastructure for carbon credit markets, providing the rails for buying, selling, and retiring carbon credits on-chain. Its Carbon Bridge tokenizes credits from registries like Puro Earth into TCO2 tokens, carbon pools such as CHAR (biochar) bundle credits into liquid reference tokens, and retirement certificates prove offsets on-chain. Developers build on Toucan through audited smart contracts on Base, Celo, and Polygon, the toucan-sdk JavaScript/TypeScript SDK, and GraphQL subgraphs served through The Graph on six networks.

companies.name: Isometric
companies.description: Isometric is a London- and New York-based certifier of climate solutions building an AI-native, science-led registry and verification platform for the industrial economy. Founded in 2022 by Eamon Jubbawy (Onfido), Isometric certifies durable carbon dioxide removal (CDR), superpollutant abatement, and related environmental attributes against the public Isometric Standard, a library of peer-reviewed protocols spanning biochar, enhanced weathering, mineralization, direct air capture, marine CDR, biosphere pathways (such as reforestation, mangroves, agroforestry, and improved forest management), and superpollutant abatement (HFC/ODS recovery, landfill methane, rice methane). Buyers, suppliers, and integrators interact with Isometric through three primary platforms — Certify (project design, MRV data ingestion, LCA, GHG statements, validation), Registry (issuances, credit batches, deliveries, transfers, retirements, buffer pools), and Protocols (operationalized scientific methodology) — exposed via the Registry API and the Certify (MRV) Data Ingestion API. Both APIs are versioned at /v0, share a unified two-credential model (X-Client-Secret + Bearer JWT), run on sandbox and production hosts, and are accompanied by a hosted MCP server at api.isometric.com/mcp that exposes the Isometric Standard, protocols, modules, and platform documentation to AI clients such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, and VS Code Copilot. Customers include Google, Microsoft, Shopify, Frontier-aligned buyers, and Anglo American, and the registry powers credit lifecycle operations for marketplaces, intermediaries, and carbon intelligence platforms.

companies.name: Refurbed
companies.description: Refurbed is a European online marketplace for professionally refurbished electronics and other sustainable goods, headquartered in Vienna, Austria and operating across Europe. Merchants sell refurbished phones, laptops, tablets, wearables and more to consumers through the refurbed platform, and refurbed exposes public partner APIs so merchants and affiliates can integrate programmatically. The Merchant API lets sellers manage offers, prices, stock, orders, returns, refunds, shipping profiles, tickets and buyback flows, while the Affiliate Partner API exposes the marketplace catalog (markets, products, instances and BuyBox data) for affiliates. Both APIs are offered as gRPC with an equivalent HTTP/JSON transport, defined by published Protobuf and OpenAPI (Swagger 2.0) specifications, and are authenticated with a secret token passed in the Authorization header.

companies.name: Greenly
companies.description: Greenly is a Paris-headquartered (with offices in London and New York) carbon accounting platform focused on small and mid-sized businesses, helping companies measure, reduce, and report their greenhouse-gas emissions across Scope 1, 2, and 3. The platform automates carbon footprint calculations from accounting, expense, supplier, energy, and cloud data; produces regulator-aligned Bilan Carbone, GHG Protocol, CSRD, CBAM, EUDR, SBTi, CDP, TCFD/IFRS, EcoVadis, and California climate disclosure deliverables; supports product-level LCA; recommends supplier alternatives; and offers a marketplace for verified carbon-offset projects. Greenly also exposes a developer-facing Carbon Analytics REST API (v1.5, hosted at api.greenly.earth) historically built by Offspend, which banks and fintechs use to enrich bank-card transactions with per-purchase CO2 emissions, classify spend into purchase categories, surface lower-carbon alternatives, and book offset volumes against vetted projects — sandbox and production environments are available with API-key authentication on request to contact@greenly.earth.

companies.name: WinCL
companies.description: WinCL (윈클) is a Korean integrated carbon-management platform that helps enterprises calculate greenhouse-gas emissions, produce climate disclosures and reports, and offset their footprint end-to-end. It combines WinCL Monitoring (emissions accounting and climate disclosure), a WinCL Marketplace for buying globally certified carbon credits (Verra, Gold Standard) and I-REC renewable-energy certificates, a WinCL Reward marketing layer, and consulting services. The WinCL API (api.wincl.io, 271 operations, Bearer JWT) exposes wallet, credit box, certificate box, product, order, Stripe/KCP payment, and Hedera on-chain minting/offset operations so customers can embed carbon purchasing and credit retirement directly into their own applications.

companies.name: Crusoe
companies.description: Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI cloud and energy infrastructure company. It builds and operates purpose-built data centers powered by renewable and alternative energy sources, and exposes that infrastructure as Crusoe Cloud: a high-performance compute platform optimized for AI training and inference on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. The Crusoe Intelligence Foundry provides managed inference for open-source and custom-tuned models (DeepSeek, Llama, Nemotron, and others). Crusoe Cloud ships a full REST API, a CLI, SDKs, a Terraform provider, and a cookbook of code samples. Public developer documentation is hosted at docs.crusoecloud.com with the API rooted at api.crusoecloud.com/v1alpha5.

companies.name: Ellipsis Drive
companies.description: Ellipsis Drive is a cloud-native spatial data management platform that lets teams upload, store, process, share, and serve raster, vector, and 3D point-cloud geospatial data through a single interoperable interface. Uploaded files are automatically processed into high-performance Tile Pyramid Archives (rasters) and Paged Vector Tiles (vectors) and served through standard OGC protocols (WMS, WMTS, WFS, WCS, XYZ, and vector tiles) alongside a REST API v3 with Bearer-token and OAuth2 authorization. Official SDKs and integrations cover Python, R, and JavaScript, plus plugins for QGIS, ArcGIS (JS, Pro, and Server), Mapbox GL, Leaflet, React-Leaflet, and Power BI. The platform offers storage-based pricing, license-free data sharing and consumption, subscriptions for selling spatial data, and both instant SaaS and private self-hosted deployments.

companies.name: Bonneville Power Administration
companies.description: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is a federal agency within the U.S. Department of Energy that markets wholesale electrical power from federal hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest. BPA also operates and maintains about three-quarters of the high-voltage transmission in the Pacific Northwest. The agency provides publicly available GIS data, energy statistics, and operational data through its data hub and web services.

companies.name: NOAA ERDDAP
companies.description: NOAA Environmental Research Division Data Access Program (ERDDAP) is a free, publicly accessible REST API and data server that provides a simple, consistent way to search, subset, and download gridded and tabular oceanographic, meteorological, and climate science datasets in a wide variety of common file formats.

companies.name: Univers
companies.description: Univers (formerly Envision Digital) is a Singapore-headquartered company building "The Platform for Physical AI" — its EnOS platform runs real-time, autonomous operations across energy grids, buildings, transportation, and industrial manufacturing, managing over 1,000 GW of energy assets and 400M+ connected sensors and devices for 800+ enterprise customers in 45 countries. EnOS exposes open APIs for device connection, models, assets, time-series data, alerts, and data subscription, consumed through the EnOS Application Portal and Developer Console with access-key/secret-key request signing, and ships first-party device and service SDKs for Java, Python, C, Node.js, .NET, and Go.

companies.name: Enviance
companies.description: Enviance (now Cority Enviance) is an environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance-management SaaS platform. Originally an independent cloud environmental-compliance vendor, Enviance was acquired by Cority and its product now ships as "Cority Enviance." The platform manages regulatory requirements, compliance tasks, emissions and environmental events, chemicals and materials inventories, documents, workflows, and reporting for enterprises in regulated industries. Its EMS REST API (the "Cority Enviance App API") exposes 250+ operations across 39 service areas — Activity, Chemical, Material, Compliance, Requirement, Event, Task, Workflow, Document, Report, Portal, Bulk data, SCIM identity, and more — for building custom interfaces and integrating Enviance with corporate and third-party systems.

companies.name: Breathe Battery Technologies
companies.description: Breathe Battery Technologies is a UK battery software company, spun out of Imperial College London in 2019, that builds physics-based battery simulation, cell design, and adaptive charging software for OEM and cell engineering teams. Its API-delivered products — Breathe Design (cell design), Breathe Simulate (validated performance and degradation modelling), and Breathe Charge (embedded adaptive charging, shipped in Volvo EVs) — are consumed through first-party Python client libraries (breathe-simulate, breathe-design) and MATLAB/Simulink integration, backed by a token-authenticated cloud service. The company is venture-backed (Speedinvest among its investors) and profiled in the API Evangelist network for its developer-facing, programmatically accessible battery engineering platform.

companies.name: Environmental Protection Agency
companies.description: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) provides multiple public data APIs covering environmental records, air quality monitoring, UV forecasts, and internal data holdings. These services enable State and local governments, federal agencies, researchers, and the public to access environmental data about air, water, and land.

companies.name: MSCI
companies.description: MSCI is a leading provider of critical decision support tools and services for the global investment community, publishing indexes, ESG and climate ratings, risk analytics, and real estate and private asset data. The MSCI Developer Community at developer.msci.com catalogs thirty-plus REST APIs spanning index performance and constituents, ESG data and reports, sustainability and climate on-demand data, risk and instrument analytics, portfolio optimization, real estate performance, and private capital metrics, alongside an official Python SDK and the MSCI Connector, a Model Context Protocol server listed in the Claude connector directory.

companies.name: Ernst & Young (EY)
companies.description: Ernst & Young (EY) is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating as a global network of member firms branded under "EY" and coordinated by Ernst & Young Global Limited (EYG). EY reports a workforce of roughly 400,000 people spanning approximately 150 countries. The firm's stated purpose is "Building a better working world" and it organizes delivery across a small set of professional service lines — Assurance, Consulting, Strategy & Transactions (branded as EY-Parthenon, covering both Strategy and Transactions and Corporate Finance), Tax, Law, Technology, Managed Services, and People & Workforce Services — plus EY Private (services for privately-held and entrepreneur-led businesses) and EY Sustainability. Industry coverage is organized into eight sectors: Industrials & Mobility, Consumer Products & Retail, Energy & Resources, Financial Services, Government & Infrastructure, Health & Life Sciences, Private Equity, and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. EY's flagship technology initiative is EY.ai, positioned as an enterprise-scale "agentic AI unifying platform" backed by alliances with NVIDIA, Microsoft, IBM, SAP, ServiceNow and others. Adjacent platform brands include EY Nexus (a sector-tailored business transformation platform marketed primarily to financial services), EY Studio+ (customer experience / growth), EY Ecosystems (partnership network), and EY wavespace (innovation centers). EY's research-publishing surface is the EY Insights portfolio, organized around topic areas (AI, Finance, Geostrategy, People and Workforce, Risk, Sustainability, Technology, EY Transformation) and flagship recurring series including the CEO Outlook, EY Megatrends, Global IPO Trends, the Private Equity Pulse, Work Reimagined, the Climate Action Barometer, and the Nature Action Barometer, plus EY Podcasts and EY Webcasts. Project Everest — the proposed split of EY's audit and consulting businesses — was publicly cancelled in April 2023, and EY continues to operate as an integrated multi-line professional services organization. EY does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, public REST APIs, or a consumer-facing API pricing surface at the global corporate level. The only first-party EY GitHub organization that is publicly discoverable is EYBlockchain (github.com/EYBlockchain, ~28 public repositories, ~160 followers, blog URL blockchain.ey.com), which hosts EY's open-source zero-knowledge cryptography and privacy-preserving blockchain work, anchored by the Nightfall optimistic-rollup family (Nightfall_3 in JavaScript / Nightfall_4 Community Edition in Rust) and the Starlight Solidity-to-zApp transpiler, alongside supporting libraries such as Timber, Poseidon, halo2-lib, snark-verifier, plonkish, algebra, and ZoKrates wrappers, plus product brands EY Blockchain Analyzer (Reconciler and Smart Contract & Token Review) and the EY OpsChain Suite (Traceability, ESG, Contract Manager).

companies.name: EcoCart
companies.description: EcoCart is a sustainable-commerce platform that embeds climate contributions, shipping protection, and returns management directly into the e-commerce checkout experience. It lets merchants calculate and offset the carbon footprint of orders, offer package protection, provide returns and cashback incentives, and communicate their sustainability story across the customer journey. EcoCart reports helping over 2,000 merchants mitigate more than 400 million pounds of greenhouse gases. The platform integrates with major e-commerce systems and exposes a developer API (hosted on Stoplight at api.ecocart.io) plus a first-party React component library for embedding sustainable-checkout surfaces into storefronts. EcoCart is backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: AuditBoard
companies.description: AuditBoard (rebranded in 2026 as Optro) is an AI-powered GRC (governance, risk, and compliance) SaaS platform used by more than half of the Fortune 500 to run their audit, risk, and compliance programs. Its connected-risk suite spans Controls Management (SOX), OpsAudit (operational/internal audit), RiskOversight (enterprise/operational risk), CrossComply (IT risk and cybersecurity compliance), ESG, RegComply (regulatory compliance), and AI Governance. Optro exposes a developer platform at developer.auditboard.com (a login-gated ReadMe portal) for programmatic access, plus documented integrations with systems such as ServiceNow, Workiva, and Microsoft 365. AuditBoard was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from its public web surface; the API reference itself sits behind an end-user login, so no public OpenAPI is captured.

companies.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
companies.description: The International Energy Agency (IEA) provides a REST API for accessing global energy statistics, renewables data, CO2 emissions factors, monthly electricity generation data, oil market reports, and energy policy information. The IEA API enables programmatic access to authoritative energy data covering 150+ countries and offering up-to-hourly real-time emissions factors alongside comprehensive historical datasets.

companies.name: CHAOSS
companies.description: CHAOSS (Community Health Analytics in Open Source Software) is a Linux Foundation project that develops metrics, methodologies, software, and practitioner guides for measuring and improving open source community health and sustainability. It produces a metrics catalog organized into focus areas (Common, DEI, Risk, Value, Evolution) and metrics models, along with open source software (Augur, 8Knot, GrimoireLab) that ingests data from Git, GitHub, GitLab, mailing lists, and other community platforms to compute the metrics. CHAOSS-aligned SaaS services such as OSS Compass and Bitergia Analytics also expose the metrics for adopters who do not want to host the software themselves.

companies.name: AES Corporation
companies.description: The AES Corporation is a Fortune 500 global energy company that generates and distributes electrical power. AES operates a diverse portfolio of renewable, thermal, LNG, and battery storage facilities across multiple countries, serving utilities, industrial facilities, and end users. AES is the largest global supplier of clean energy to corporations in the Americas and operates 34.7 GW globally with $12.2 billion in annual revenue. The company serves 18.7 million household equivalents through utilities in Indiana, Ohio, and El Salvador. AES also co-founded Fluence Energy, a leading energy storage and software platform company.

companies.name: Satellogic
companies.description: Satellogic is an Argentine-founded, U.S.-listed (NASDAQ: SATL) vertically integrated Earth observation company that designs, builds, and operates its own NewSat constellation to deliver sub-meter, high-frequency multispectral and hyperspectral satellite imagery. Its commercial platform Aleph unifies archive search, tasking, analysis, and delivery into a single web and API experience, available in both the legacy Aleph V1 (Tasking, Archive, Analysis, Delivery APIs) and the unified Aleph V2 Orders API. Satellogic also markets Aleph Observer for persistent daily monitoring of designated sites, Constellation-as-a-Service for priority and large-scale tasking, and Space Systems for customers who wish to purchase and operate their own Mark V class satellites. Imagery is delivered via API, FTP, and a reseller network, with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials authentication against auth.platform.satellogic.com and product APIs under api.satellogic.com.

companies.name: Sharethrough
companies.description: Sharethrough is a human-centric programmatic advertising platform and one of the largest independent omnichannel ad exchanges, offering REST APIs for publishers and advertisers to manage native, display, and video ad placements through SSP/DSP integrations, real-time bidding via OpenRTB, programmatic reporting, and sustainability-focused media buying with Scope3 Climate Shield certification.

companies.name: Waste Connections
companies.description: Waste Connections is the third-largest integrated provider of solid waste services in North America, serving approximately nine million residential, commercial, and industrial customers across 46 U.S. states and six Canadian provinces. The company provides non-hazardous waste collection, transfer, disposal, and recycling services, primarily in exclusive and secondary markets. Waste Connections is investing in AI-powered dynamic routing and expanding customer connectivity features through its online customer portal.

companies.name: Bureau of Land Management
companies.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is a U.S. government agency responsible for managing vast stretches of public lands across the country, primarily focused on activities like outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production, aiming to sustain the health and diversity of these lands for future generations.

companies.name: Climacell
companies.description: Climacell (styled ClimaCell) was a Boston-based weather-intelligence startup that pioneered a "Weather of Things" approach — deriving hyperlocal precipitation and atmospheric conditions from wireless-signal attenuation, connected devices, and its own proprietary numerical weather model — and exposed it through a developer-facing REST weather API. Backed by Canaan Partners among others, the company rebranded to Tomorrow.io in 2020 and its legacy climacell.co domain now 301-redirects to www.tomorrow.io. The surviving product is the Tomorrow.io v4 Weather API, which supersedes the original ClimaCell v3 API and exposes 60+ hyperlocal data layers (core weather, air quality, pollen, fire, flood, lightning, maritime, aviation, road) with realtime, forecast, historical, map-tile, and webhook-alert access. This profile is the historical ClimaCell identity; the enriched, live provider record lives in the api-evangelist tomorrow-io repository.

companies.name: AerisWeather
companies.description: Comprehensive weather data REST API providing forecasts, observations, severe weather alerts, historical data, satellite imagery, and maps for global locations. Now operating as Xweather (acquired by Vaisala in 2022), the platform offers 60+ endpoints covering current conditions, forecasts up to 15 days, air quality, lightning, maritime weather, road conditions, wildfires, earthquakes, and tropical cyclones. Developer toolkits are available for JavaScript, Python, iOS, and Android.

companies.name: Eliq
companies.description: Eliq provides energy data and analytics APIs for utilities and energy app developers. The platform combines a decade of analytics and machine learning trained on millions of homes to deliver consumption insights, disaggregation, forecasting, peak detection, tariff comparison, and customer segmentation.

companies.name: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement
companies.description: The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) works to promote safety, protect the environment, and conserve resources offshore through vigorous regulatory oversight and enforcement.

companies.name: Climate-X
companies.description: Climate X is a London-headquartered climate risk analytics company that translates physical climate hazards into financial loss metrics for banks, insurers, asset managers, real estate firms, and consultancies. Its Spectra product models a range of physical climate hazards across roughly 1.5 billion global assets under multiple emissions scenarios and time horizons, delivering asset- and portfolio-level annual loss, probability, and severity estimates via a web platform, CSV export, BI tools, and an Enterprise API. Additional products include Adapt (adaptation capex and ROI), Carta (global asset location and exposure mapping), and Adaptation Finance. Climate X is ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 14001 certified and a certified B Corporation. The Enterprise API is currently gated behind sales, so no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal is available.

companies.name: Deloitte
companies.description: Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services organizations, operating through a network of member firms coordinated by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited (DTTL). The organization spans approximately 150 countries and territories, has more than 180 years of history (founded 1845), and serves roughly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. Deloitte organizes delivery across four primary service lines — Audit & Assurance, Consulting, Tax, and Legal — plus specialized cross-functional practices including Business Process Solutions and Global Employer Services. Consulting offerings cover Customer, Cyber, Engineering / AI & Data, Enterprise Technology & Performance, Finance Transformation, Human Capital, Strategy & Transactions, and Risk / Regulatory & Forensic. Deloitte Digital is the technology-and-experience practice with alliances spanning Salesforce, Adobe, SAP, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, Shopify, Sitecore, and Genesys, and accelerators such as FrontOffice Advantage, Revenue Advantage, Agentic Marketing Cloud, CreativEdge, Blueprint, Content Studios, and TrustID. The organization serves six industries divided into twenty sectors: Consumer; Energy, Resources & Industrials; Financial Services; Government & Public Services; Life Sciences & Health Care; and Technology, Media & Telecommunications. Deloitte Insights is the organization's research-publishing surface, organized into eight research centers — Cross-Industry, Economics, Consumer, Energy & Industrials, Financial Services, Government & Public Services, Life Sciences & Health Care, and Tech, Media & Telecom — producing flagship series including Tech Trends, Global Human Capital Trends, Digital Media Trends, TMT Predictions, FSI Predictions, the Weekly Global Economic Outlook, and the annual Industry Outlooks. The Deloitte AI Institute drives applied-AI research and points of view. Deloitte does not publish a public developer API or open developer portal at the corporate level. The Deloitte US Consulting GitHub organization is small (5 visible repositories, mostly archived upstream forks; the original artifact is `beacon`, a first-party web-analytics packaging library in TypeScript). Reader-facing distribution flows through MyDeloitte (personalized content + newsletter subscriptions), Dbriefs (live webcasts with CPE credit), the Deloitte Insights Magazine, and the YouTube channel; no public RSS index page was discoverable on www.deloitte.com at the path published in legacy archives.

companies.name: Copernicus Marine
companies.description: The EU Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS), operated by Mercator Ocean International, provides free and open access to authoritative information on the state of the global ocean and European regional seas. The service delivers ocean physical and biogeochemical data through multiple APIs covering temperature, salinity, sea level, currents, sea ice, and marine ecosystem variables from satellite observations, in situ measurements, and numerical model reanalysis and forecast products. Data can be accessed programmatically via the Copernicus Marine Toolbox (Python API and CLI), the OGC-compliant Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) for visualization, and the Catalogue Service for the Web (CSW) for product discovery. All services require a free Copernicus Marine account, except the CSW which is fully open, and there are no data volume quotas or download limits.

companies.name: Ecologi
companies.description: Ecologi is a Bristol, UK climate action platform and B Corp founded in 2019 that lets individuals and businesses fund verified reforestation, carbon avoidance, carbon removal, and habitat restoration projects through monthly subscriptions, pay-as-you-go purchases, and a public Impact API. The platform has funded over 95 million trees, avoided 4.1 million tonnes of CO2e, removed 61,000 tonnes of CO2e, and restored 102,000 square metres of habitat across projects in Guatemala, Brazil, Kenya, Uganda, India, Pakistan, the UK, and beyond. Ecologi serves over 16,000 businesses with an end-to-end Measure, Reduce, Report (3Rs) workflow aligned to SBTi, GHG Protocol, ISO 14064-1, SECR, and CSRD, and exposes a public REST API (and a Zapier app and Shopify app) so any business can automate climate impact per order, per signup, per invoice, or per workflow event. The platform is delivered as a browser-based SaaS application (login at ratedpower.enverus.com) and reports 64,000+ projects designed and 5.1 TW of simulated capacity. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal is published; enterprise automation access exists only behind the authenticated application. This profile was seeded as a Techstars portfolio lead and has been run through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Remoov
companies.description: Remoov is a San Francisco-based full-service removal, resale, donation, and recycling company that helps households and businesses declutter by picking up unwanted furniture and goods, then reselling them on consignment (via reperch.com), donating them to charities, or recycling them responsibly. Customers schedule a pickup, receive a quote, and earn a share of resale proceeds. Remoov also serves realtors, stagers, property managers, and living communities as partners. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; Remoov publishes a consumer web app and help desk but no public developer API.

companies.name: Resourcify
companies.description: Resourcify (Resourcify GmbH) is a Hamburg, Germany based digital platform for waste management and circular-economy operations, describing itself as "the operating system for a circular future." Its cloud software helps enterprises digitize and optimize their waste streams end to end - automating waste and recycling operations, optimizing cost, CO2 and recycling rates, tracking compliance, and running take-back systems - across manufacturing, construction, retail, healthcare, and airports. The platform connects waste producers with a network of recyclers and haulers, captures waste data and documentation, and reports on sustainability and material recovery. Resourcify is backed by Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

companies.name: Kayrros
companies.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

companies.name: Enervee
companies.description: Enervee operates an AI-powered white-label marketplace platform that helps utilities and government energy programs scale energy efficiency across 39 million-plus households in North America. Its stack spans a utility-branded online store for efficient appliances and equipment across 40-plus product categories (HVAC, water heaters, heat pumps, smart thermostats, EV chargers), the Enervee Score - a proprietary 0-100 energy-efficiency rating updated daily - Eco Financing embedded lending at checkout through national bank partners, and Instant Rebates that automatically stack utility, government, and manufacturer incentives at checkout. Enervee is a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public security, trust, and identity posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Makersite
companies.description: Makersite is an AI-powered Product Lifecycle Intelligence platform that helps manufacturers manage product sustainability, cost, and compliance by connecting products to deep-tier supply chain, material, and chemical data. The platform automates lifecycle assessments (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) calculations, supports eco-design and cost optimization, and produces regulatory reporting such as EU Taxonomy and CBAM. It integrates with enterprise CAD, ERP, and PLM systems (PTC Windchill, Siemens Teamcenter, Autodesk, ANSYS). Makersite is a portfolio company of Partech. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

companies.description: Arka is a custom packaging company that lets ecommerce brands design, order, and ship eco-friendly custom boxes, mailers, and sustainable packaging online. Arka offers low minimums, fast turnaround, and plug-in integrations with commerce platforms including Shopify, BigCommerce, and Square so merchants can reorder packaging alongside their fulfillment workflow. Arka's storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface — a published /llms.txt, an agentic-discovery sitemap, OIDC/OAuth 2.0 discovery for the Shopify Customer Account API, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled here as part of the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Cloover
companies.description: Cloover is a climate-fintech company building an all-in-one, "Shopify of energy" platform for the residential renewable-energy transition. It connects the stakeholders of home energy - installers, homeowners (prosumers), manufacturers, energy providers and investors - so small and mid-sized installation firms can sell, quote, finance and manage solar panels, home batteries, heat pumps and EV charging in a single package. The platform pairs installer sales and operations software with embedded financing and energy management, and offers homeowners flexible subscription and financing options. Founded in 2023 and operating primarily in Germany, Austria and wider Europe, Cloover has raised sizeable seed and Series A equity plus a large debt facility and is backed by QED Investors, MMC Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital and others.

companies.name: Goodr
companies.description: Goodr is an Atlanta-based sustainable surplus food management and hunger-relief logistics company founded in 2016 by Jasmine Crowe-Houston. Goodr helps businesses divert edible and inedible food waste from landfills by scheduling pickups, donating surplus edible food to local nonprofits, and providing donors with the tax deductions and impact reporting tied to those donations. Alongside its food-waste solutions, Goodr runs hunger-relief programs including pop-up grocery markets, meal delivery, student snackpacks, and community grocery stores. The company reports more than 30 million meals served and 4 million pounds of food diverted from landfills for enterprise partners such as Amazon, Google, NASA, and Fulton County. Goodr operates through a partner portal rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sunairio
companies.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

companies.name: Clarity AI
companies.description: Clarity AI is a sustainability technology and fintech company that provides AI-powered extra-financial intelligence for financial decision-making. Its platform delivers ESG risk ratings, climate and physical-risk analytics, regulatory-compliance reporting (EU Taxonomy, SFDR, MiFID II, ESMA fund naming, Pillar 3), impact and UN SDG alignment, and retail-banking climate engagement tools. Clarity AI reports coverage of 300K+ listed and private companies, 450K+ funds, and 400+ sovereigns, and serves asset managers, asset owners, banks, wealth managers, and corporates. The company exposes its data through a web application, data feeds, APIs, and emerging AI agent / MCP integrations, though its developer surface is gated behind an enterprise platform login rather than a public developer portal. Clarity AI is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

Retailers can launch a white-label resale marketplace with no upfront cost and integrate with any e-commerce platform. Founded in 2023 and backed by $7.4M in pre-seed and seed funding led by Earlybird VC, Brandback reports a 9.5% average conversion-rate lift with customers including Replay Jeans and Sandqvist.

companies.name: Archive
companies.description: Archive is a brand-owned resale and recommerce technology platform, founded in 2021, that lets forward-thinking global brands launch and scale profitable, sustainable resale businesses. Its circularity platform spans branded recommerce storefronts, peer-to-peer marketplaces, trade-in (online and in-store), take-back, warranty and repair, a resale warehouse management system (WMS), a unified product catalog, a dynamic pricing engine, and analytics — reclaiming supply through returns, past-season inventory, consumer listings, and in-store trade-ins. Archive serves 50+ brands across 10+ countries, including The North Face, lululemon, Peloton, New Balance, Dr. Martens, Fjällräven, Oscar de la Renta, Hanna Andersson, and Faherty. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (with Energize Capital leading its $30M Series B), and has raised $54M to date.

companies.name: Certa
companies.description: Certa (operated by Opinr, Inc. d/b/a Certa) is an AI-native third-party risk management (TPRM) and compliance platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle — onboarding, due diligence, contract management, continuous compliance monitoring, and offboarding — in a single no-code system. Founded by Jag Lamba and headquartered in Saratoga, CA, Certa serves Fortune 500 companies (Honeywell, Uber, Mars, Box, Quantcast) across 120+ countries and 17 languages. The platform covers all risk domains — operational and resilience, infosec and cyber, compliance and legal, financial and credit, reputational, geopolitical, and ESG and ethical risk — via its Studio no-code process designer, Certa Connect (130+ native integrations), and embedded AI agents. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools. External integration is available through an enterprise external API surfaced from the platform; no public OpenAPI or developer portal is published as of this profile.

Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. The managed-service platform also supports B Corp certification, CSRD readiness, SOC 2 and AI-governance compliance, and tracking of regulations such as California SB 253 and SB 261. Greenplaces is venture-backed by Felicis and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; the company publishes a managed product (app.greenplaces.com) but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Noda
companies.description: Noda (formerly Infogrid) is an agentic AI platform for commercial real estate building operations. It functions as an always-on AI virtual building engineer that connects to a portfolio's building management systems (BMS), IoT, weather, and utility data, continuously detects faults and energy waste, identifies root causes, generates quantified savings recommendations, and executes authorized setpoint and load adjustments — tying every action to measured, audit-ready ROI. The platform processes 100M+ data points daily and reports 15-25% annual energy reduction across deployed assets. Trusted by owners and operators of 400M+ square feet including Hilton, JLL, CBRE, Macerich, Cousins, DivcoWest and Salesforce. ISO 27001 certified and hosted on AWS in the United States. Backed by Northzone. Noda exposes no public developer API; onboarding is enterprise/demo-based.

companies.name: Plans
companies.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

companies.name: Schüttflix
companies.description: Schüttflix is a Gütersloh, Germany based digital logistics platform for the construction industry, describing itself as the first digital logistics hub to connect construction companies, building-material suppliers, disposal companies and carriers. The marketplace digitizes the full workflow from ordering bulk materials (sand, gravel, crushed stone) through transport dispatch to the delivery note, and adds construction-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling services. Schüttflix operates as a neutral marketplace ("we don't compete, we connect") spanning 4,000+ suppliers and disposers, 6,800+ partner carriers and 33,000+ vehicles, delivered primarily through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public API. It is a portfolio company of HV Capital, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Sirius
companies.description: beSirius is an Amsterdam-based AI platform for the critical minerals and metals value chain. It builds a continuously verified digital Twin of every supplier, mapping each company's data to the frameworks, questionnaires, and regulations its buyers, auditors, and regulators require - including CSDDD, CMRT/EMRT/AMRT conflict-minerals reporting, EcoVadis, CDP, S&P CSA, UN Global Compact, LME Passport, and the Consolidated Mining Standard Initiative (CMSI). The platform automates supplier due diligence, sustainability and ESG data collection and verification, certification readiness, customer KYC, and ratings improvement across mining, processing, and trading supply chains, reducing manual audit and disclosure effort. beSirius is backed by Techstars and other investors.

companies.name: Normative
companies.description: Normative is a Stockholm, Sweden-based carbon accounting and ESG reporting software company helping enterprises measure, report, and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions across scopes 1, 2, and 3. Its platform combines a library of more than 349,000 region- and sector-specific emission factors with workflows for product carbon footprint (PCF), supply chain engagement, Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) target setting, Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) disclosure, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reporting. Calculations are built to the GHG Protocol and independently verified by TÜV SÜD against ISO/IEC 25051. Customers include Vodafone, Hertz, Hitachi Rail, and Flying Tiger Copenhagen, and every account is paired with a named, GHG Protocol-certified Climate Strategy Advisor rather than a traditional support helpdesk. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscriptions plus advisory services; Normative does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and its GitHub organization (normative-io) currently exposes no public repositories.

companies.name: Terrascope
companies.description: Terrascope is a Singapore-headquartered climate-tech and sustainability software company building an enterprise carbon measurement, management, and decarbonization platform. Launched in 2022 after being incubated and spun out of Olam Group (a Temasek-linked Singapore agribusiness), and led by former Google and AWS executive Felipe Daguila, Terrascope serves large food, agriculture, retail, and manufacturing enterprises that need to quantify Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions across their operations, products, and supply chains. The platform centers on four core modules: Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) for organization-level inventories, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) for product-level lifecycle emissions, Supplier Engagement for Scope 3 primary-data collection, and Climate Reporting for audit-ready disclosure. Terrascope's differentiator is its AI-assisted data ingestion layer (built on Amazon Bedrock) that reduces measurement cycles by roughly 80% versus manual baselines, intelligent emissions factor matching with FLAG (Forestry, Land, and Agriculture) breakdowns, data gap-filling claiming 92% accuracy versus supplier data, and a curated library of over 20,000 decarbonization best practices used to power what-if scenario modeling and ROI-ranked recommendations. The platform supports the GHG Protocol (including Land Sector and Removals guidance), SBTi FLAG, CDP (Terrascope is a CDP Gold Accredited software provider), TCFD, California SB253, and Australia's S2 climate disclosure regimes. Notable customers include Kellanova, Princes Group, iNova Pharmaceuticals, Mandai Wildlife Group, Olam Food Ingredients, Tetra Pak, Mitsubishi, Japan Tobacco, and Kagome. Investors include Olam Group and Plug and Play Tech Center. Terrascope is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS — there is no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or open-source release. The github.com/terrascope organization exists but has no public repositories, and docs.terrascope.com is not publicly resolvable. Integration with customer ERP, procurement, and energy systems is handled through bespoke implementation engagements rather than self-serve developer onboarding.

companies.description: Bright is Mexico's leading residential and commercial solar energy provider, founded in 2014 (Y Combinator W15) by Jonah Greenberger. Often described as "Sunrun for the developing world," Bright combines financing and software to let homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar and battery energy storage (BESS) at no upfront cost. The company operates a marketplace connecting a network of local installers, distributors, and retail promoters with customers, and offers financing models such as solar PPAs and leasing schemes. Bright's public web presence is a Wix-hosted marketing site (thinkbright.mx) covering its industrial, commercial, and home solutions, success cases, and 24/7 energy monitoring technology. It exposes an agent-facing surface via an llms.txt and a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint, but publishes no first-party developer/REST API.

companies.description: Better Origin is a UK-based agritech company decarbonizing the food chain by converting food waste into sustainable, locally produced animal feed. Its core technology is a fully automated, AI-controlled containerized insect farm that breeds black soldier fly larvae to consume food waste and produce nutrient-rich insect-based ingredients for pet food, poultry feed, and aquaculture. The systems are remotely monitored and controlled by software and require no specialist knowledge from operators. Better Origin is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

The current product line covers AI logo design, packaging design, AI product photography, image editing, packaging ranges, flavor/variant ranges, brand moodboards, and (announced) product mockups and social ads. Sourceful is ISO 42001 certified for AI management. companies.description: Equilibrium Energy is a venture-backed clean energy technology company building PowerOS, an agentic AI platform for the power and energy sector. The platform is designed to solve the extreme data and systems fragmentation across the power tech stack, uniting enterprise data, models, and systems under a common ontology and code frameworks so that power companies can deploy power-specific AI with guardrails they control. PowerOS bundles enterprise agents (trader and research copilots, app co-developers, data ingestion and transformation), configurable application suites (portfolio management, portfolio construction, development workbenches, middle and back office), and reusable core services (optimization, forecasting, risk, grid and market fundamentals, trading). The company's Mission Control product is in invite-only beta. Equilibrium Energy is backed by DCVC and is headquartered in the United States. Its Esperesso hyperspectral imagers capture more than 100 contiguous spectral bands spanning roughly 400 to 1000 nm, which Esper turns into mineralisation maps that identify lithium, rare earths, gold, nickel, cobalt and alteration zones for critical-mineral exploration — faster, cheaper and greener than traditional ground surveys. Founded in 2021 in Melbourne, Victoria by Iqbal and Joey Lorenczak, Esper sells custom area-of-interest mineral maps and a pre-built Northern Territory mineral map. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and code-repository surface.

companies.description: Involve Space is an Italian stratospheric aerospace company building real-time Earth intelligence. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. companies.name: EnerVenue

companies.name: Helion Energy
companies.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

companies.name: Dispatch Goods
companies.description: Dispatch Goods is a reusable-packaging and reverse-logistics company that offers returnable containers and insulated bags as an alternative to single-use and compostable packaging for direct-to-consumer meal kits, grocery delivery, and food-service operations. The company handles the full circular loop — packaging, collection, washing, and redistribution — and markets its reusable system as a cheaper and lower-impact substitute for cardboard, gel packs, and insulation, citing reductions in water use and CO2 equivalent emissions. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

companies.name: Inviscid AI
companies.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

companies.name: Kairos Aerospace
companies.description: Kairos Aerospace is a methane-detection company founded in 2014 in Sunnyvale, California that provides cost-effective, high-frequency aerial methane detection for the oil and gas industry. Its patented LeakSurveyor spectrometer is flown over upstream and midstream infrastructure to image methane plumes, and proprietary software turns those flights into actionable emissions data so operators can find, prioritize, and fix leaks. The company rebranded as Insight M in March 2024 and was subsequently acquired by Zeitview. Kairos Aerospace was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is an identity record rather than an API catalog entry.

companies.name: Kintep (Jiangsu Kintep Environmental Protection Co., Ltd.)
companies.description: Jiangsu Kintep Environmental Protection Co., Ltd. (江苏康泰环保股份有限公司), founded in 2011 and headquartered in Taizhou, Jiangsu, China, is a national high-tech enterprise that designs, manufactures, sells, and services new-type environmental-protection equipment and complete turnkey solutions. Kintep focuses on solid-liquid separation and intelligent sludge / pollutant collection and treatment. Its KINTEP product line includes multi-disc (stacked-screw) sludge dewatering machines, integrated automatic chemical dosing units, dense-phase belt sludge deep-dewatering machines, high-efficiency fully-automatic filter-press systems, Lamella sedimentation tanks, and screw presses. The company operates seven national customer-service centers (Shenzhen, Wuhan, Chongqing, Xi'an, Tianjin, Shanghai, Yixing) and exports to customers worldwide. Kintep is a physical industrial-equipment manufacturer and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Libra Robotics
companies.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

companies.name: Sense
companies.description: Sense is a Cambridge, Massachusetts energy-intelligence company that builds a residential energy monitor and machine-learning platform for real-time whole-home electricity disaggregation. The Sense Monitor installs in a home electrical panel, samples voltage and current at one million times per second, and uses signature-based machine-learning models to identify individual appliances and loads behind a single point of measurement. The Sense iOS, Android, and web apps surface device-level usage, always-on load, solar production, time-of-use cost, and goal tracking to homeowners. For utilities and grid operators, Sense embeds its disaggregation software into next-generation AMI 2.0 smart meters through partnerships with meter manufacturers such as Landis+Gyr, providing grid-edge visibility, fault detection, load-management, demand-response, and virtual-power-plant enablement. Sense also runs a partner program for smart-device integration with thermostats, EV chargers, heat pumps, and home-service providers. Sense has not released an official public developer API; community developers maintain reverse-engineered, unofficial clients in Python, Node.js, and Home Assistant against an undocumented and unsupported endpoint. Sense's revenue model is hardware sales of the consumer monitor and licensing of its disaggregation software to utilities and meter OEMs.

companies.name: Soma Energy
companies.description: Soma Energy is an AI-powered energy intelligence platform that optimizes how power is produced, stored, and consumed. Founded by former Amazon and technology leaders, it coordinates power generation, battery storage, and large energy consumers such as data centers. Its Intelligence Platform combines three products: AI Trader, which automates energy procurement, hedging, and dispatch for independent power producers (IPPs); BESS Dispatcher, which manages battery energy storage systems; and Load Optimizer, which coordinates data-center workloads with grid conditions to cut energy costs and turn facilities into flexible grid assets. Soma Energy is an early-stage company backed by Uncork Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, developer platform, or documentation.

companies.name: Axionorbital Space
companies.description: AxionOrbital Space is a San Francisco Bay Area startup (Y Combinator Winter 2026) building foundation models for continuous Earth observation through clouds and darkness. Its flagship model, ORION, converts Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into high-resolution, photorealistic optical imagery in real time using deterministic one-step diffusion, overcoming the limitation that traditional optical satellites are unusable roughly 70% of the time due to weather and night cycles. The technology targets 24/7 situational awareness for defense and intelligence, commodities and financial analytics, disaster response, agriculture, and climate monitoring. Founded in 2025 by Dhenenjay Yadav (CEO, former ISRO ML engineer) and Atharva Peshkar (CTO, PhD, CU Boulder / Harvard VCG). At the time of profiling the company is pre-product with no public API, developer portal, or specifications published; this record captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Buildscience
companies.description: BuildScience Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2015) was a PropTech startup based in Mountain View, California that built an operating-system platform for commercial buildings. Its software let building owners and facility operators deploy customized building-management solutions intended to reduce operational costs while improving tenant satisfaction, and the company reported deploying in a one-million-square-foot Class A office building. As of the 2026 enrichment pass the company appears dormant: the buildscience.com domain no longer serves a live product (the host returns a CloudFront default certificate that does not match the domain and a broken origin), no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be located, and the organization's single public GitHub repository was last updated in January 2020. This profile is retained as a verified-identity network record; no API artifacts could be enriched because the provider publishes no live API.

companies.description: First Solar is a leading global provider of comprehensive photovoltaic (PV) solar energy solutions, designing and manufacturing thin-film solar modules. No public developer portal or open APIs have been identified at this time.

companies.name: ICF (ICF International)
companies.description: ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI), formerly ICF International, is a global consulting and digital services firm headquartered in Reston, Virginia, delivering management, technology, and policy consulting to US federal agencies, state and local governments, utilities, and commercial clients. ICF serves markets spanning government, energy, environment, infrastructure, transportation, health, education, social programs, public safety, and disaster management, with approximately 9,000 employees worldwide. The firm has invested in an in-house AI offering branded "ICF Fathom," but no public REST APIs, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation have been identified. ICF's work is delivered under contract rather than through a productized developer platform.

companies.name: Johnson Controls
companies.description: Johnson Controls is a global diversified technology and multi-industrial leader serving customers in over 150 countries, providing products, services, and solutions for buildings (HVAC, fire, security, building automation), energy storage, and connected building platforms (Metasys, OpenBlue). No public, self-service developer portal or OpenAPI is currently published; partner and customer integrations are typically delivered through the OpenBlue and Metasys product lines.

companies.name: Kairos Power
companies.description: Kairos Power is an Alameda, California-based advanced nuclear fission company developing the KP-FHR (Kairos Power Fluoride salt-cooled High-temperature Reactor), a Generation IV reactor design that uses TRISO (tri-structural isotropic) fuel pebbles cooled by molten fluoride salt (FLiBe) at low pressure and high temperature. Kairos Power is building Hermes, a low-power demonstration reactor at the East Tennessee Technology Park in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, which became the first non-light-water reactor authorized for construction by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in over 50 years (construction permit issued December 2023). A second unit, Hermes 2, will pair two reactors with a 28 MWe electricity-generating turbine. In October 2024 Google signed a corporate power purchase agreement with Kairos Power for up to 500 MW of nuclear electricity from multiple small modular reactors, with the first deployment targeted by 2030 and additional capacity through 2035 — the first corporate PPA for new advanced nuclear in the United States. The company's revenue model is reactor sales, electricity PPAs, and federal cost-share partnerships (DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program). Kairos Power is privately held, does not expose a public developer API or SDK, and operates under NRC regulatory oversight as a safety-critical nuclear licensee.

companies.name: Kuva Space
companies.description: Kuva Space is a Finnish space-data company headquartered in Espoo that operates a fleet of hyperspectral Earth observation microsatellites and delivers AI-driven planetary intelligence through its Kuva Sense platform. Founded in 2016 (originally as Reaktor Space Lab) by Tuomas Tikka and Janne Kuhno in collaboration with Reaktor, the company designs, builds, and operates its own 6U CubeSat-class spacecraft carrying a patented in-orbit tunable Fabry-Perot 2D snapshot hyperspectral imager. Its operational Hyperfield-1A (launched August 2024 on SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg) and Hyperfield-1B (launched June 2025) cover the 475–950 nm VNIR range with up to 160 tunable spectral bands at 25 m spatial resolution and a 50 km swath from a 500 km polar sun-synchronous orbit. The larger 70 kg Hyperfield-2 microsatellite, scheduled for H2 2026, expands coverage to 450–1,650 nm at 15 m resolution with an additional 3.6 m GSD RGB camera. By 2030 Kuva Space plans to grow the constellation to roughly 100 satellites to enable sub-daily revisit anywhere on Earth. Onboard AI handles cloud filtering, spectral band alignment, and compression so that downlinked products feed directly into Kuva Sense, where automated analytics generate insights-as-a-service for agriculture (crop identification, yield forecasting, harvest timing), aquaculture (water quality, algal bloom detection, biomass), environment and carbon (sequestration monitoring, deforestation, pollution tracking), and safety and security (vessel detection and tracking, illegal activity warning, rapid change detection). Kuva Space is part of the European Space Agency InCubed-co-funded HYPERFIELD program, was awarded a €1.8M ESA Civil Security from Space contract within the SMART-CONNECT consortium to demonstrate rapid hyperspectral insights for crisis response, and in 2026 signed a Letter of Intent with SSC Space to strengthen Nordic space capabilities. The commercial model is subscription-based insights-as-a-service rather than pay-per-pixel imagery sales, with current access offered through the Kuva Sense Early Adopter Program; the company markets "robust APIs and customizable data formats" for system integration but does not currently publish open public API reference documentation, an OpenAPI specification, or a self-service developer portal. The only public engineering surface is the open-source kuva-data-processing Python toolkit (kuva-metadata, kuva-reader, kuva-geometry) on GitHub and PyPI, which reads Kuva GeoTIFF-based L0/L1AB/L1C/L2A data products and their metadata sidecars.

companies.name: Nanogrid
companies.description: Nanogrid was an Oakland, California software startup founded in 2017 by Patrick Sheehan (CEO), Jon McKay (Co-Founder & CPO), and Dan Lopuch (Co-Founder & CTO) that built software to determine the value of residential solar, battery storage, and electric vehicles for homeowners. Its platform simulated, estimated, and optimized these distributed energy resources and captured the operational synergies between the devices. A 500 Startups (500 Global) Batch 25 company, Nanogrid raised roughly $150K from 500 Global and Plug and Play Tech Center before being acquired by clean-energy company Arcadia on April 22, 2021. The company no longer operates independently and its nanogrid.tech domain no longer resolves; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead record. (Not to be confused with the separate nanoGrid energy-data platform at nanogrid.com.)

companies.name: Orbital Insight
companies.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

companies.name: Peerby
companies.description: Peerby is a Dutch peer-to-peer sharing platform that lets neighbors borrow and rent everyday goods from one another instead of buying them new. Through its website and mobile apps, members request or list items such as tools, party and event equipment, electronics, bicycles, and household goods, then arrange local pickup and return. Positioned as an affordable, convenient, and more sustainable alternative to ownership, Peerby aims to reduce consumption and waste by unlocking the underused items already sitting in people's homes. Backed by Techstars, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Peerby operates a consumer single-page web application and native apps; it does not publish a public developer/API program, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or a .well-known discovery surface at this time.

Its Ward 250 test reactor is a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy, the San Rafael Energy Research Center, and the State of Utah. Founded by Isaiah Taylor and backed by Initialized Capital, the company publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

A 500 Global portfolio company, XING Mobility publishes no public developer API or API documentation as of July 2026.

companies.name: Alsym Energy
companies.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Amprius Technologies
companies.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

companies.name: Arcstone
companies.description: Arcstone is a Singapore-based digital manufacturing technology company (founded 2013) that helps enterprises digitalize and gain real-time transparency across their shop floors and supply chains. Its product family spans arc.essentials (a lightweight Manufacturing Execution System for SMEs), arc.ops (a modular, next-generation MES for large enterprises), arc.net (multi-tier supply chain visibility), arc.studio (a low-code enterprise app and integration platform), arc.green (sustainability tracking), and arc.ai (an AI control tower for managed AI workforce deployment). Arcstone serves precision engineering, FMCG, mining, semiconductor, plastics, and biomedical manufacturers, and was named a Gartner Cool Vendor in Manufacturing Operations in 2022. The company is backed by 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; this profile carries the identity and infrastructure signals harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: BlackSky
companies.description: BlackSky Technology (NYSE: BKSY) is a Herndon, Virginia headquartered real-time space-based intelligence company that operates a high-revisit Earth observation constellation and delivers AI-enhanced tactical ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance) imagery and analytics to defense, intelligence, and global security customers. BlackSky's flagship product is the Spectra platform — a cloud-based intelligence hub that provides on-demand satellite tasking, sub-90-minute imagery delivery, automated AI-driven object detection and change monitoring, archived imagery access, and a secure tasking and delivery API. The company operates Gen-2 satellites at 83 cm resolution and a newer Gen-3 constellation delivering 35 cm class very-high-resolution imagery with infrared sensors, inter-satellite links, and on-board AI processing, manufactured at BlackSky's facility in Tukwila, Washington. Commercial offerings include BlackSky ON-DEMAND (flexible global tasking) and BlackSky ASSURED (dedicated, contracted persistent monitoring capacity). BlackSky's Spectra tasking and imagery API is integrated into partner platforms including Esri ArcGIS, UP42, and the STAT (Satellite Tasking API) community spec, however the API is access-controlled for vetted defense, intelligence, and enterprise customers and is not exposed as a public self-service developer portal — there is no public Spectra developer documentation site, OpenAPI specification, or open SDKs at the time of this entry. The customer revenue model is subscription-based Spectra ON-DEMAND and ASSURED contracts, Mission Solutions custom engagements, and through marketplace partners.

companies.name: Ch4 Global
companies.description: CH4 Global is a climate-technology company working to reduce methane emissions from livestock at gigatonne scale. Its flagship product, Methane Tamer, is a feed supplement made from Asparagopsis red seaweed that has been shown to cut enteric methane emissions in cattle by up to 90 percent. In January 2025 the company began production at what it describes as the world's first commercial-scale Asparagopsis growing facility, its EcoPark in Louth Bay, South Australia, using a proprietary pond-based cultivation system to lower production costs. CH4 Global is a deep-tech and agriculture-focused company backed by DCVC; it operates as a physical-product and climate-impact business rather than a software or API provider. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.
