companies.name: Coolant
companies.description: Coolant (Coolant Climate, Inc.) is a climate-technology startup building AI-powered forest monitoring and carbon measurement from consumer-grade drone imagery. Its "3D spatial intelligence" platform reconstructs high-resolution 3D forest models from ordinary drone footage (DJI Mini, Mavic) and applies computer vision to measure biomass, tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), tree counts, species, and growth rates — delivering LiDAR-grade accuracy at a fraction of the cost. The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Darling Ingredients
companies.description: Darling Ingredients is a global developer and producer of sustainable natural ingredients from edible and inedible bio-nutrients, creating products for the food, pet food, feed, fuel, bioenergy, and fertilizer industries. Darling operates Diamond Green Diesel as a renewable diesel joint venture with Valero, and brands such as Rousselot (gelatin and collagen), Sonac, CTH, and EnviroFlight. Darling does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Fervo Energy
companies.description: Fervo Energy is a next-generation geothermal power company headquartered in Houston, Texas, that generates carbon-free, always-on electricity through enhanced geothermal systems (EGS). Founded in 2017 by Tim Latimer and Jack Norbeck, Fervo adapts horizontal drilling, distributed fiber-optic sensing, and advanced subsurface data analytics from the oil and gas industry to make geothermal energy viable in previously uneconomic locations. Its projects include the Project Red pilot in Nevada and the flagship 500 MW Cape Station development in Beaver County, Utah. Fervo trades on Nasdaq under the ticker FRVO and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network surfaced from the DCVC portfolio; Fervo Energy is a physical energy-infrastructure company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Form Energy
companies.description: Form Energy is a long-duration energy storage company headquartered in Somerville, Massachusetts and Weirton, West Virginia. Its flagship product is an iron-air battery designed to store electricity for up to 100 hours, intended to enable utilities and grid operators to firm renewable generation across multi-day weather events, replace aging fossil-fueled peakers, and defer transmission and distribution upgrades. The company manufactures its battery at Form Factory 1, a 550,000-square-foot facility built on the former Weirton Steel mill site that employs roughly 400 people. Form Energy also publishes Formware, a grid-modeling software suite used by utilities to plan resource portfolios that include multi-day storage. Notable customers and partners include Georgia Power, Xcel Energy, Great River Energy, Dominion Energy, PG&E, New York Power Authority, and Crusoe Energy (a 12 GWh agreement to firm power for AI data centers). Form Energy does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK; engagement is through utility sales, partnership, and policy channels.

companies.name: Fourier
companies.description: Fourier is an energy technology company building on-site, on-demand hydrogen production systems. Its core product is a modular, scalable device that generates hydrogen where it is needed, removing the transport and storage barriers of conventional hydrogen supply. Fourier targets three application areas: long-duration distributed storage for renewable energy, alternative fuels for heavy transportation, and cleaner feedstock for chemical and manufacturing industries. The company commercially launched its onsite hydrogen system in late 2025 and raised an $18.5M Series A led by Paramark Ventures and General Catalyst. Fourier is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software developer surface.

companies.description: Graphic Packaging International is a Fortune 500 global manufacturer of sustainable, paperboard-based consumer packaging. Products include folding cartons, multipack cartons, foodservice packaging (cups, lids, to-go containers), microwave and ovenable packaging, paperboard canisters, and packaging machinery. Markets served include food, beverage, foodservice, household, personal care, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, pet care, beauty, and e-commerce. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

companies.name: Helion Energy
companies.description: Helion Energy is a fusion energy company headquartered in Everett, Washington pursuing a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed-configuration (FRC) approach that uses a deuterium-helium-3 fuel cycle and direct electricity recovery rather than steam turbines. The company is on its seventh-generation prototype, Polaris, which achieved first plasma in 2024 and is targeted to demonstrate net electricity production from fusion. Helion's prior machines include Trenta, the sixth-generation prototype that reached fusion-relevant plasma temperatures, and Hercules, an earlier device. Orion is Helion's planned first commercial fusion power plant, with a publicly announced 2028 target for delivering electricity to Microsoft under what the companies describe as the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement; a second customer agreement is in place with steelmaker Nucor. Helion is led by co-founder and CEO David Kirtley, CTO Chris Pihl, Chief Scientist George Votroubek, and co-founder Anthony Pancotti. Investors include Sam Altman (chair), Dustin Moskovitz, Reid Hoffman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Mithril Capital, Capricorn Investment Group, Peter Thiel, and others. Helion does not publish a public developer API or SDK.

companies.name: Holtec International
companies.description: Holtec International is a privately held American supplier of equipment and systems for the nuclear, solar, geothermal, and fossil power-generation industries. The company is best known for its spent-fuel storage and transport casks (HI-STAR, HI-STORM, HI-STORE CISF), decommissioning services through Holtec Decommissioning International (HDI), and its in-development SMR-300 small modular reactor — a roughly 320 MWe two-loop pressurized water reactor with an 80-year design life. Holtec is currently pursuing the first-ever restart of a permanently shut-down U.S. commercial nuclear power plant at Palisades in Michigan, which is also designated as the first deployment site for the SMR-300. The company runs manufacturing facilities in Camden, NJ, Pittsburgh, PA, and Orrville, OH, and partners with Hyundai Engineering & Construction (HDEC) on SMR-300 detailed design and full-scope plant construction.

companies.name: Mycotech
companies.description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Neoplants
companies.description: Neoplants is a French climate-biotechnology company building genetically and microbially engineered houseplants that capture and metabolize indoor air pollutants. Its consumer product line pairs bioengineered pothos plants with an enhanced root microbiome ("Power Drops") to remove volatile organic compounds such as formaldehyde, benzene, toluene and xylene from indoor air. Backed by Partech and other climate investors, Neoplants operates as a direct-to-consumer brand rather than an API provider. This API Evangelist profile was created from a venture-portfolio lead; an enrichment pass confirmed the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface as of July 2026.

companies.name: NuScale Power
companies.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

companies.name: Rubicon
companies.description: Rubicon (formerly NYSE: RBT) is a waste, recycling, and sustainability technology company founded in 2008. It went public in 2022 via a SPAC merger with Founder SPAC at a pro forma valuation of roughly $1.7 billion, branding itself a "digital challenger" to the traditional waste-hauling industry with a marketplace connecting waste generators to independent haulers plus the RUBICONSmartCity fleet-and-routing platform used by more than 70 municipalities. Operating Status: the company subsequently faced severe financial distress - layoffs and debt restructuring in 2023, a June 2024 NYSE delisting, and a May 2024 divestiture of its entire fleet technology and smart-city business unit (RUBICONSmartCity, RUBICONPro, RUBICONPremier) to Rodina Capital for roughly $68 million plus a possible $12 million earnout; those assets were subsequently absorbed by Routeware. In early 2025 Rubicon deregistered its securities and became a privately held company, majority-owned by Jose Miguel Enrich through MBI Holdings, and remains the subject of shareholder litigation over the change-of-control terms. The surviving company operates as a smaller enterprise waste brokerage and sustainability-data business built around the RUBICONConnect platform (service, equipment, pickup, and cost visibility for enterprise customers such as Chipotle and FedEx), alongside RUBICONRegWatch compliance tooling, sustainability reporting, technical advisory services, and the Rubicon Now on-demand dumpster-rental service in a handful of cities. rubicon.com publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no OpenAPI specification. The only discoverable API artifact tied to the rubicon.com domain is a "Routeware Smartcity Public Api" Swagger UI hosted at a dev subdomain (haulerpublic-api.dev.aws.rubicon.com) - leftover infrastructure from the divested fleet/smart-city business - which returned a 503 Service Unavailable on every check during this review and is not publicly documented or reachable. Any hauler or municipal system integration Rubicon references (for example, connecting to city 311 systems) is negotiated per partner and gated behind sales and onboarding rather than exposed through self-serve developer documentation. Pricing across RUBICONConnect and Rubicon's enterprise services is entirely quote-based and negotiated per contract; no public pricing, tiers, or rate limits are published. This entry is maintained as an honest stub pending any future public API surface.

companies.name: SINAI Technologies
companies.description: SINAI Technologies is a San Francisco–headquartered enterprise SaaS company providing a Decarbonization Intelligence platform for carbon management, sustainability planning, and ESG compliance. The platform unifies organization-wide emissions accounting, climate transition planning, climate financial planning, and execution management so industrial enterprises can measure, report, and reduce Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions using science-based methodologies. Core modules include Carbon Accounting & Reporting, the Climate Transition Planner (with marginal abatement cost curves and scenario modeling), the Climate Financial Planner, and Execution & Management for tracking decarbonization projects. SINAI's Decarbonization Intelligence Portal layers Tableau-based dashboards, AI-powered bulk data ingestion, and AI Emissions Match (which maps unstructured emissions data to emission factors) on top of the underlying carbon ledger. The platform is designed around major reporting frameworks including CDP, TCFD, SEC climate disclosure, CSRD, CBAM, California SB 253 / SB 261, Brazil SBCE, and Brazil CVM resolutions 217 and 218, and is SOC 2 compliant with TÜV SÜD ISO 14064 verification. Customers include Siemens Energy, ArcelorMittal, Harley-Davidson, Emirates, Natura &Co, Minerva Foods, Wilson Sons, BRK Ambiental, and Japan's largest bank MUFG. SINAI states publicly that it can connect to enterprise customer systems through APIs to automate roughly 70% of emissions data ingestion, but it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, public API reference, or a GitHub organization — its API surface is delivered as a private integration capability negotiated with enterprise customers rather than a self-serve developer product.

Backed by Nvidia, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, NFX and others, Starcloud is building a roadmap of Starcloud-1 through Starcloud-4 satellite compute platforms. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a space-compute infrastructure company and lead for future enrichment.

companies.name: Supercritical
companies.description: Supercritical is a London-based carbon removal marketplace founded in 2021 by Michelle You and Aaron Randall, the team behind Songkick. The company builds the market infrastructure that turns carbon dioxide removal (CDR) commitments into delivered tonnes, connecting corporate buyers with vetted suppliers of durable, engineered, and nature-engineered carbon removal. Supercritical's marketplace covers the major durable CDR pathways — biochar, BECCS, enhanced weathering, direct air capture (DAC), DAC with ocean storage, woody biomass sinking, and bio-oil — with published per-tonne pricing and live availability data. The platform layers a proprietary 118-point vetting protocol on top of supplier listings, spanning climate science, environmental impact, delivery risk, and social benefits, and reports that 84% of assessed projects fail to meet its standards. Supercritical also provides supply sourcing and creation services to originate new CDR projects, buffer-pool-based delivery-risk mitigation, and policy and science advisory work (its team advises SBTi on CDR guidance). Customers include Virgin Atlantic, The Economist Group, Rothschild & Co, XTX Markets, and Tide, with reported coverage of roughly 80% of the global durable CDR market and 1.3M tonnes contracted across 200+ corporate buyers and 600+ tracked suppliers. The business is funded by Lightspeed Venture Partners, MMC Ventures, and GreenCode Ventures. Supercritical does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; transactions, supplier discovery, and pricing data are delivered through its hosted marketplace, advisor relationships, and contracted buyer accounts.

companies.name: TAE Technologies
companies.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

companies.description: Verra is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit standards body that develops and manages the world's leading certification programs for climate action and sustainable development. Verra also operates the Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (CCB), the Sustainable Development Verified Impact Standard (SD VISta), the Plastic Waste Reduction Standard (PWRP), the Scope 3 Standard Program, and the Jurisdictional and Nested REDD+ (JNR) framework. The Verra Registry at registry.verra.org is the system of record for projects, methodologies, issuances, retirements, and the AFOLU pooled buffer account across these programs; project documentation, public comment periods, and credit-lifecycle records are all surfaced through that registry. Verra recently launched VCS Version 5, modernizing program operations, strengthening safeguards, and clarifying credit rights. Verra does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or GitHub organization; programmatic data access is limited to the registry's web interface and filtered report exports, and there is no open-source code or machine-readable spec catalog associated with the organization.

X-energy's fuel subsidiary, TRISO-X, is building a commercial TRISO fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. companies.name: Electroflow
companies.description: Electroflow Technologies is a United States deep-tech company (founded 2023, headquartered in San Bruno, California) developing an electrochemical direct lithium extraction (DLE) process that pulls lithium from dilute North American brines containing under 200ppm lithium using renewable electricity and minimal chemicals. Its cell uses anodes that absorb lithium ions from brine on one pass and release them into a carbonate solution on the reverse pass, producing battery-grade lithium carbonate that is reacted with iron and phosphate to make lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode powder domestically — a three-step route versus the traditional ten-step process, targeting LFP material at roughly 40% below Chinese producers. The company raised a $10M seed round in October 2025 led by Union Square Ventures with Voyager Ventures, Fifty Years, and Harpoon Ventures, and counts Breakthrough Energy among its backers. Electroflow is a hardware and battery-materials company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

companies.name: Zap Energy
companies.description: Zap Energy is a Seattle, Washington fusion energy company pursuing commercial fusion power via the sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch — a compact, magnet-free pulsed-power approach in which a flowing column of deuterium plasma is compressed (pinched) to fusion conditions inside a roughly two-meter metal tube, with shear in the axial flow stabilizing the pinch in place of the heavy superconducting magnets used by tokamak and stellarator designs. Founded in 2017 by Benj Conway, Brian A. Nelson, and Uri Shumlak as a spinout of University of Washington and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory research, the company has developed a lineage of devices — ZaP, ZaP-HD, FuZE, FuZE-Q, and FuZE-3 — culminating in 2024 with Century, a 100-kW-scale repetitive pulsed-power test platform with liquid-metal walls intended to demonstrate plant-relevant technologies. In November 2025 FuZE-3 reported plasma electron pressures of 830 MPa (1.6 GPa total), the highest pressure measured in any sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch and a marker on the path to scientific energy gain (Q>1). Zap Energy was selected for the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program in May 2023 and received DOE approval of the preconceptual design of its Fusion Pilot Plant. The company has raised over $325 million across Series A–D from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, Energy Impact Partners, Chevron Technology Ventures, Shell Ventures, DCVC, Valor Equity Partners, and Addition. As of April 2026, Zabrina Johal serves as CEO with Conway as President, and the company has expanded its mandate to also pursue small modular fission alongside its fusion roadmap. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; Sylvamo operates primarily through B2B sales channels and investor and corporate communications channels.

companies.name: Chart Industries
companies.description: Chart Industries is a leading global manufacturer of highly engineered equipment servicing multiple market applications in clean energy and industrial gas. The company provides cryogenic equipment, process technologies, and aftermarket services for hydrogen, LNG, biogas, CO2 capture, and traditional industrial gases. Chart Industries does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

companies.name: AMEE
companies.description: AMEE (Avoiding Mass Extinctions Engine, also styled Avoidance of Mass Extinctions Engine) was a London-based environmental-intelligence company founded around 2005 by Gavin Starks out of UK firm Dgen. It ran an open web-service API and cloud database that standardized carbon-emissions and energy-consumption data across 150+ countries, letting applications apply government emission factors to tracked activities. AMEE powered carbon calculators and footprinting for clients including Google, Morgan Stanley, Radiohead, Sun Microsystems, and UK and Irish government programs (notably the Act on CO2 campaign). It raised roughly $7.5M from Union Square Ventures, OATV (O'Reilly AlphaTech Ventures), The Accelerator Group, and Amadeus Capital Partners. AMEE was acquired by Pi (PredictX) in late 2015 / early 2016 and no longer operates as an independent company; the amee.com domain currently returns HTTP 502 with no live API or developer surface.

companies.name: Anthemis Group
companies.description: Anthemis Group is a London-based venture capital and asset management firm founded in 2010 by Amy Nauiokas (Group CEO) and Sean Park (Group CIO), both former capital-markets executives. Anthemis invests to "architect the digital economy," concentrating on financial technology and its adjacencies: embedded finance, payments and banking infrastructure, insurtech, wealthtech, crypto and digital assets, climate and agtech finance, and applied AI for financial services. The firm invests primarily at pre-seed, seed, Series A and early Series B, writing checks generally in the ~$2M-$3M range, and pairs venture investing with an advisory and platform practice aimed at systematically transforming financial services. Anthemis is headquartered in London with additional presence in New York, Geneva, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Dallas, manages roughly $500M in assets, and has backed 300+ companies including Betterment, eToro, Carta, Pipe, TrueLayer, Tide, Currencycloud, Atom Bank and The Climate Corporation.

companies.name: Atomico
companies.description: Atomico is a London-headquartered European venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Niklas Zennstrom, co-founder of Skype and Kazaa. Atomico partners with Europe's most ambitious technology founders from the earliest stages to pre-IPO across two dedicated teams: a Venture team that invests predominantly at Series A alongside occasional Seed opportunities, and a Growth team that invests from Series B to pre-IPO. In September 2024 the firm closed its largest ever fundraise, $1.24 billion across two funds - a $754M Atomico Growth VI vehicle and a $485M Atomico Venture VI vehicle - bringing total capital raised across seven funds to more than $5 billion. Growth-stage checks typically range from roughly $10M to $50M+. Atomico invests broadly across enterprise software, fintech, consumer, health, AI, developer tools, infrastructure, industrial and climate technology, with an explicit thesis that European technology has come of age. The firm operates offices in London, Paris, Berlin and Stockholm and is known for backing category-defining companies including Klarna, Stripe, Supercell, Graphcore, DeepL, Pipedrive, Truecaller, Wellhub, Lilium, Compass, Hinge Health and Sorare. Atomico also publishes the annual State of European Tech report, the definitive data-driven analysis of the European technology ecosystem.

companies.name: DCVC (Data Collective)
companies.description: DCVC (Data Collective) is a deep-tech venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in Palo Alto and San Francisco, California. Founded and led by managing partners Matt Ocko and Zachary Bogue, DCVC backs entrepreneurs using computational and AI-driven approaches to solve trillion-dollar problems in the real world across sectors that have often seen little material progress in decades. The firm invests from early through growth stages across AI, compute and quantum, computational biology and chemistry, cybersecurity and defense, energy and climate, finance and insurance, industrial transformation and advanced manufacturing, next-gen agriculture, space, TechBio and TechMed. Across 13+ funds DCVC manages roughly $4B in assets under management (self-reported / press), making it one of the larger dedicated deep-tech franchises. Notable portfolio outcomes include companies spanning fusion energy, carbon transformation, robotics, drug discovery, and data infrastructure.

companies.name: Disclosure Requirements
companies.description: Disclosure Requirements are the regulatory and legal obligations for organizations to reveal specific information to stakeholders, regulators, and the public. These requirements span financial disclosures (SEC, IFRS), sustainability and ESG reporting (CSRD, ESRS, IFRS S1/S2, TCFD, GRI, SASB), privacy notices (GDPR, CCPA), and corporate governance, helping ensure transparency and accountability across markets and jurisdictions.

companies.name: Energy and Utilities
companies.description: Energy and Utilities is a topic profile in the API Evangelist Network cataloging the API surfaces that move data across the modern electricity, gas, and water value chain. It indexes utility data integration APIs, grid and wholesale market operator APIs, federal energy data programs, renewable energy research APIs, weather APIs that drive grid demand and solar forecasting, EV charging interoperability protocols, and the Green Button family of customer energy data standards. The repo provides a baseline catalog plus shared semantics (JSON Schema, JSON-LD, vocabulary, examples) for the meter reading / energy data point that ties every one of these surfaces together.

companies.name: EQT Ventures
companies.description: EQT Ventures is the early-stage venture capital business within EQT Group, launched in 2016 and operating out of Stockholm with investment-advisory offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, and the United States (San Francisco / New York); the funds themselves are domiciled in Luxembourg. The firm is a sector-agnostic, conviction-led lead investor that backs what it calls "Generation-Defining Companies" from pre-seed and seed through Series A and B, writing checks that reported ranges place between roughly EUR 1M and EUR 75M (most commonly EUR 2M-50M) and following on as companies scale. EQT Ventures has raised approximately EUR 2.3B across three funds (EQT Ventures I, II, and III) and is staffed largely by ex-founders and operators who provide hands-on support in addition to capital. Its focus spans AI, SaaS and developer tools, fintech, healthtech, climate and deeptech, robotics and aerospace, gaming, and consumer/marketplaces. Notable investments include Wolt, Depop, Typeform, AnyDesk, Netlify, Fly.io, Einride, Small Giant Games, Kry, and Beamery.

companies.name: Fifth Wall
companies.description: Fifth Wall is a venture capital firm founded in 2016 by Brendan F. Wallace and Brad Greiwe and headquartered in Los Angeles, California, with additional offices in New York, San Francisco, and London. It is the largest investment firm focused on technology for the built environment ("PropTech") and real estate, investing across the venture and growth stages into companies that make buildings and the physical world smarter, safer, more sustainable, and more energy efficient. The firm spans sub-themes including proptech, construction technology, residential real estate, fintech for real estate, smart buildings, logistics, and a dedicated climate/decarbonization strategy. Fifth Wall's distinctive model pairs its portfolio companies with a network of roughly 115 strategic limited partners — major real estate owner-operators such as CBRE, Hilton, Hines, Marriott, Public Storage, Related, and Starwood Capital — to drive strategic partnerships and distribution. With over $3 billion in assets under management and nearly 170 portfolio companies, Fifth Wall has backed category leaders including Opendoor, Procore, ServiceTitan, Blend, Hippo, SmartRent, and Bilt Rewards.

companies.name: Homebrew
companies.description: Homebrew is a San Francisco-based seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2013 by Hunter Walk (a former product leader at Google and YouTube) and Satya Patel (a former VP of Product at Twitter, partner at Battery Ventures, and product leader at Google). Named after the Homebrew Computer Club, the firm practices high-conviction, concentrated seed investing, taking board-level positions and acting as an extension of the founder's team. Roughly 90% of its investments are pre-seed and seed, with initial checks in the $100K-$500K range and the ability to follow on up to $25M+ in later rounds. Homebrew backs mission-driven founders working on large, urgent, and valuable problems across fintech, AI/ML, healthcare, climate, defense, logistics, real estate, and consumer, focused on companies operating in the Americas. After a decade of institutional funds that backed companies such as Chime, Plaid, Gusto, and Mercury, Homebrew announced in 2021 that it would stop raising outside LP capital and invest only its own money going forward under the banner "Homebrew Forever."

companies.name: Initialized Capital
companies.description: Initialized Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2012 by Garry Tan, Alexis Ohanian, and Harjeet (Harj) Taggar, with offices in San Francisco and New York. The firm is hyper-focused on the seed stage, typically investing before a startup's success strikes other investors as inevitable and favoring companies that have raised little to no prior capital. Rather than thematic investing, Initialized centers its thesis on strong founding teams and acts as a de facto extended founding team from 0 to 1, providing operational support across product design, engineering, recruiting, storytelling, go-to-market, and Series A fundraising. It invests broadly across enterprise SaaS, consumer, marketplaces, fintech, crypto, healthcare, climate, hardware, real estate, and frontier/AI technology. As of 2021 the firm had raised more than $3.2B across its funds and has backed 200+ companies, including 28 unicorns such as Coinbase, Instacart, Cruise, Flexport, Reddit, Opendoor, Rippling, and Patreon, with portfolio companies creating an aggregate of over $200B in market value.

companies.name: Khosla Ventures
companies.description: Khosla Ventures is a Menlo Park, California venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla. The firm backs bold, early, and impactful ventures, favoring contrarian deep-tech bets with world-class teams and a conviction-driven approach that deliberately accepts a high failure rate to capture transformative outcomes. Khosla invests across seed, early (Series A/B), and growth stages through its Seed Fund, Main Fund, and Opportunity (growth) Fund, writing checks that range from small seed positions to large growth rounds. Focus sectors span artificial intelligence, enterprise and consumer software, financial services and fintech, robotics and frontier/deep tech, aerospace and defense, climate and sustainability (clean energy, fusion, materials, agriculture), and digital health, medtech, diagnostics, and therapeutics. The firm manages roughly $16 billion in assets as of 2025 and is known for early investments in OpenAI, Stripe, Square/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Affirm, Impossible Foods, GitLab, Okta, Rocket Lab, and QuantumScape. Headquarters are at 2128 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA, with a primarily United States geographic focus and select global investments.

companies.name: Kindred Ventures
companies.description: Kindred Ventures is a San Francisco-based, earliest-stage venture capital firm founded in 2014 by Steve Jang and led today as a partnership with Managing Partners Steve Jang and Kanyi Maqubela. The firm backs visionary and relentless founders building the future with technology and science, investing primarily at the pre-seed and seed stage and often partnering with entrepreneurs before a company is even formed. Kindred runs a deliberately concentrated, high-touch model of roughly 25 companies per fund, and has backed 100+ startups whose aggregate market capitalization now exceeds $200B. It invests across AI and new computing, crypto/web3, fintech, consumer, health and wellness, climate tech, mobility and logistics, and developer tools and infrastructure. With around $600M in assets under management, notable investments and exits include Uber, Coinbase, Poshmark, Reddit, Postmates, Blue Bottle Coffee, Perplexity, Tala, Magic Eden, dYdX, and PlayAI (acquired by Meta in 2025).

companies.name: Northzone
companies.description: Northzone is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 in Oslo and now headquartered in London, with additional offices in New York, Stockholm, Berlin and Amsterdam. The firm partners with founders across the United States and Europe from Seed through Growth, positioning itself as a single long-term partner from the first check all the way to IPO, with check sizes ranging from roughly $1M to $50M. Over nearly three decades Northzone has raised 13 funds, backed more than 250 companies, produced 18 unicorns and 14 IPOs, and reports $3.1bn+ in assets under management; its most recent flagship vehicle raised approximately €1bn. Northzone invests broadly across AI, enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthcare, climate and energy, and infrastructure and developer tools, and is known for early backing of category creators including Spotify, Klarna, Trustpilot, Kahoot!, Personio, TrueLayer, Avito and iZettle. The firm supports portfolio companies through a Platform team and a network of 500+ operators drawn from companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Stripe.

companies.name: Obvious Ventures
companies.description: Obvious Ventures is a San Francisco-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2014 by Ev Williams, James Joaquin, and Vishal Vasishth, investing in entrepreneurs building "world positive" companies that solve humanity's biggest problems through technology. The firm invests across three thesis pillars: planetary health (sustainable energy, food, mobility, climate), human health and longevity (healthcare, biotech, wellness), and economic health (fintech, the future of work, robotics, and inclusive systems). Obvious writes approximately 10 new checks per year, typically $5M to $12M into seed and Series A rounds, deliberately keeping fund sizes small enough that a single durable public company can return an entire fund. It closed its fifth fund at $360,360,360 in early 2026 and has backed 90+ companies since inception, including Beyond Meat, Planet, Gusto, Recursion, Devoted Health, Diamond Foundry, and Proterra. Obvious is a Certified B Corporation headquartered at 190 Pacific Avenue, San Francisco, CA.

companies.name: Open Charge Map
companies.description: Open Charge Map is the global public registry of electric vehicle charging locations, established in 2011 as a non-commercial, community-driven project. The platform maintains a crowdsourced dataset of 300,000+ charging points worldwide, combining manually entered data with imported open data from government registries and charging networks. The REST API enables developers to search and retrieve POI (Points of Interest) data on EV charging stations, including location details, equipment specifications, connection types, operator information, and user-submitted check-ins and photos. Data can be filtered by geographic coordinates, bounding box, country, operator, connection type, charging level, and operational status. The API is free to use with an API key registration and supports both read (GET) and write (POST) operations for contributing new charging location data.

companies.name: Social Capital
companies.description: Social Capital is a technology investment firm founded in 2011 by Chamath Palihapitiya (a former Facebook executive) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with co-founders Mamoon Hamid and Ted Maidenberg. Originally a traditional venture fund that stood out by backing healthcare, financial services, education, and other hard, regulated sectors the VC community had neglected, the firm pivoted in 2018 into a technology holding company that stopped accepting outside capital and now invests from its own permanent balance sheet of roughly $2.1B, aiming to "earn like Berkshire Hathaway and invest like the Red Cross." Its thesis targets multiple emerging $10T markets across deep tech commercialization, life sciences and drug discovery, the global energy transition, and creator-economy media. Chamath became known as the "SPAC King" for taking companies public through the Social Capital Hedosophia (IPOA-IPOF) vehicles, including Virgin Galactic, Opendoor, Clover Health, and SoFi. Notable investments include Slack, Box, SurveyMonkey, Wealthfront, Netskope, Intercom, Groq, Palmetto, Saildrone, and Relativity Space.

companies.name: Speedinvest
companies.description: Speedinvest is one of Europe's most active early-stage venture capital firms, founded in 2011 by Oliver Holle and headquartered in Vienna, Austria, with additional offices in Berlin, London, Munich, and Paris across EMEA. The firm invests from pre-seed and seed through selective growth stages, writing typical early-stage checks of roughly EUR 500K to EUR 3M (and up to around $10M in later rounds), and manages more than EUR 1.2 billion in assets under management. Speedinvest runs a specialist model built around dedicated sector teams rather than generalists: AI & Infra, Climate Tech & Industrial Tech, Deep Tech, Fintech & DeFi, Health & Bio, Marketplaces & Consumer, Growth, and Middle East, Africa & Beyond. Its "many move more" thesis pairs early capital with hands-on operational support, talent, customer introductions, and a global follow-on network. The firm backs technical founders across Europe and beyond, with a portfolio of 400+ companies including Bitpanda, Tide, GoStudent, Wayflyer, Curve, Adverity, Bitmovin, CoachHub, and Prewave.

companies.name: Stellation Capital
companies.description: Stellation Capital is a Brooklyn-based pre-seed and seed venture capital firm founded in 2021 by Peter A. Boyce II, who spent eight years at General Catalyst and co-founded its student-founder program Rough Draft Ventures. Operating under the tagline "Backing Founders At First Light" and the thesis "Present Before Proof," Stellation raised a $40M debut fund and writes first checks of roughly $250K-$2.5M, leading and co-leading rounds for "philomath" founding teams whose identities are inseparable from the problems they are solving — across AI and personal computing, fintech, consumer software, online safety, climate/energy, and consumer health. Portfolio companies include Strobe Power, Revin, Tapestry, Hopscotch (acquired by Avalara), Software Applications Incorporated, swsh, Block Party, Hearth Display, and Vybe. Stellation is also a partner fund in Foundry Group's portfolio, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. The firm publishes no APIs; this profile carries its identity and portfolio graph.

companies.name: Techstars
companies.description: Techstars is a global pre-seed startup accelerator and investor founded in 2006 by David Cohen, Brad Feld, David Brown, and Jared Polis in Boulder, Colorado, and headquartered in New York City. Operating a worldwide network of mentorship-driven accelerator programs across cities including Boulder, Boston, Chicago, New York, London, and Tokyo, Techstars runs an intensive three-month program that provides each accepted company roughly $220,000 in capital — a $20,000 convertible equity agreement for a minimum 5% of common stock plus an optional $200,000 uncapped MFN post-money SAFE (Asia-Pacific programs at ~$100,000). The firm is largely sector-agnostic but is especially active in AI/ML, fintech, SaaS, developer tools, healthcare, climate, space and defense, and critical infrastructure, and operates on its signature "Give First" philosophy. Techstars has backed more than 10,000 founders, producing dozens of unicorns and notable companies including Twilio, SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Uber, Remitly, Chainalysis, ClassPass, DataRobot, and PillPack, with portfolio companies collectively raising tens of billions in follow-on capital.

companies.name: True Ventures
companies.description: True Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Jon Callaghan and Phil Black and headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California. Operating under a "first to believe" thesis, True writes the initial institutional check and stays invested through every subsequent stage of a company's journey, concentrating on pre-seed, seed, and Series A rounds with check sizes reported in the roughly $500K-$15M range. The firm invests broadly across technology and founder-led categories including software and developer infrastructure, consumer products and internet, healthcare and life sciences, hardware and robotics, climate and energy, security, and AI. With more than $3.8B in committed capital, True has backed 1,050+ founders across 500+ companies since inception, with notable early checks into Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, Automattic/WordPress, HashiCorp, Duo Security, Sweetgreen, Bluesky, and Splice. True is known for its founder-first platform, the True University founder camps, and long-term conviction-led early ownership.

companies.name: Union Square Ventures
companies.description: Union Square Ventures (USV) is a thesis-driven, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 by Fred Wilson and Brad Burnham and headquartered at 817 Broadway in New York City. USV invests at the edge of large markets being transformed by technological and societal pressures, historically backing large networks of engaged users that are differentiated through user experience and defensible through network effects, and more recently companies that broaden access to knowledge, capital, and well-being. The firm invests primarily at Seed and Series A across three strategies — a Core fund, a Climate fund, and an Opportunity (later-stage) fund — with check sizes typically ranging from roughly $1M at seed to the low-to-mid single-digit millions at Series A. USV runs a small, collegial partnership and focuses on social media, marketplaces, developer tools, learning/education, health, fintech, web3/decentralized protocols, energy, and climate. It reports roughly $1.9B in assets under management across 14 funds. Notable investments include Twitter, Etsy, Coinbase, Stripe, Cloudflare, MongoDB, Twilio, Duolingo, Kickstarter, Stack Overflow, SoundCloud, and Carta.
